subject.title: Telegram: apiRoot local Bot API server receives updates but never dispatches to agent sessions

question: For Telegram local Bot API migration, should OpenClaw reset/scope polling offsets by `apiRoot`, rely on doctor/docs for manual reset, or keep account/token-only offsets as the runtime contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable state policy and the safe scope for tolerating `400: Logged out` during Bot API migration are compatibility-sensitive behavior choices.

options.title: Endpoint-aware runtime fix
options.body: Scope or invalidate Telegram update offsets when `apiRoot` changes, add a narrow `400: Logged out` migration tolerance, and require live local Bot API proof.

options.title: Doctor/docs reset path
options.body: Keep runtime offsets account/token-scoped and make `openclaw doctor --fix` or documentation the supported way to reset offsets when switching endpoints.

options.title: Operator-managed workflow
options.body: Leave local Bot API endpoint migration as an advanced manual workflow and document the current cleanup expectations without runtime changes.

recommendation.title: Endpoint-aware runtime fix
recommendation.body: Scope or invalidate Telegram update offsets when `apiRoot` changes, add a narrow `400: Logged out` migration tolerance, and require live local Bot API proof.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the strongest recent owner signal for the Telegram polling/spool path that would own an endpoint-aware runtime fix.
